title: Bauer’s Blast Propels Brewers to World Series Brink, Brew Crew Fans Celebrate!
body:
Milwaukee’s postseason hopes surged dramatically on Monday night as Jake Bauers delivered a clutch, seven‑run rally in the seventh inning of Game 2 of the National League Championship Series, propelling the Brewers to a 5‑4 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks and putting the club within one win of a World Series berth. The dramatic turnaround came against left‑handed ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who had been dominant all season and entered the game with a 2.01 ERA in the playoffs. Bauers’ 11‑pitch, three‑run double not only erased a 4‑2 deficit but also shifted the momentum of the series, which now stands 2‑0 in Milwaukee’s favor.

The Brewers entered the night trailing 1‑0 after a tightly contested Game 1 that saw Arizona’s offense capitalize on a late‑inning error. Milwaukee’s starter, Freddy Peralta, delivered a solid six‑innings, allowing just two runs, but the early deficit forced the Brewers to rely on their depth. After a quiet first half, the seventh inning erupted when Bauers, pinch‑hitting after a defensive shuffle, faced Yamamoto with two outs and runners on first and second. On a full count, Bauers drove a towering line drive to deep left‑center, sending the ball over the fence for a three‑run double that ignited the crowd at American Family Field and gave Milwaukee a 5‑4 lead they would not relinquish.

Bauers’ at‑bat will likely be remembered as one of the most iconic moments in Brewers history. The 11‑pitch sequence featured a blend of patience, power, and situational hitting rarely seen in postseason play. He fouled off two fastballs, worked a high‑fastball slider into a deep fly, and finally connected on a 96‑mph fastball that seemed to catch Yamamoto’s glove too late. The swing not only demonstrated Bauers’ raw power—his ninth career postseason home run—but also his poise under pressure, a quality that has eluded the franchise in previous NLCS outings.

Arizona’s response was swift but insufficient. Yamamoto, who had been flawless through six innings, surrendered his first two hits of the night in the seventh and was pulled after the double. Reliever Ryan Thompson entered to face the heart of the Brewers’ lineup, striking out three batters in a row and preserving the lead. The Diamondbacks managed a solitary run in the eighth on a sacrifice fly, but Milwaukee’s bullpen, anchored by closer Trevor Megill, shut down any further threats. Megill recorded his second save of the series, striking out the side in the ninth to clinch the win.

The victory not only gives the Brewers a commanding 2‑0 series lead but also underscores the depth of their roster. While star outfielder Christian Yelich and veteran pitcher Corbin Burnes have been the focal points of the team’s success, Bauers’ heroics illustrate the impact of role players stepping up when the stakes are highest. Manager Craig Counsell praised his bench, noting, “We have guys ready to contribute at any moment. Jake’s swing changed everything tonight, and that’s the kind of resilience we need to get to the World Series.”

Looking ahead, the Brewers will aim to close out the series in Game 3 at home, where they will rely on Peralta to pitch deep into the game and on the offense to maintain its newfound rhythm. Arizona, meanwhile, must regroup and find a way to neutralize Milwaukee’s late‑inning surge, possibly by adjusting their bullpen usage and seeking more timely hitting. If the Brewers can sustain the momentum sparked by Bauers’ unforgettable at‑bat, they stand on the brink of a historic World Series appearance, a milestone the franchise has not achieved since 1982.
